idea-plugin.name: AutoHotkey v2, TOML and DeviceTree checks
idea-plugin.description:
A DeviceTree overlay with status = "enabled" boots the node disabled and a TOML integer with a leading zero stops the parser. Neither is an editor error. 22 checks and 46 snippets across 9 language packs, running offline in the editor you already have.

Right-click in the editor (or Tools) → AutoHotkey v2, TOML and DeviceTree checks: Check This File. Each finding appears on its line with the fix. 22 rules, offline. Runs the same engine as the VS Code extension and the CLI: npx @readystack/autohotkey-toml-devicetree-snippets (Node.js 18+ required).

Free for the file you open. The whole-project sweep and the report need a licence ($29 once): getreadystack.com/tools/autohotkey-toml-devicetree-snippets
